message.content:
Sure! Below is a quick example of how you can add a comment to the IP address **192.168.1.1** on VirusTotal using your API key.  
Feel free to adapt it to your preferred language or environment.

---

### 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}'
```

> **Tip:**  
> - Replace `ABC321` with your actual API key.  
> - If you’re using a different API version, adjust the URL accordingly (e.g., `/api/v3/...`).

---

### 2️⃣ Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests
import json

API_KEY = "ABC321"
IP_ADDRESS = "192.168.1.1"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDRESS}/comments"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}

payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload))

if response.status_code == 200:
    print("Comment added successfully!")
    print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))
else:
    print(f"Failed to add comment. Status code: {response.status_code}")
    print(response.text)
```

> **What this does:**  
> 1. Builds the correct API endpoint for the IP address.  
> 2. Sets the required headers, including your API key.  
> 3. Sends the JSON payload containing the comment text.  
> 4. Prints out the response from VirusTotal.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Response Example

If everything goes well, you’ll receive a JSON response similar to:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "some-comment-id",
    "type": "comment",
    "links": {
      "self": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/comments/some-comment-id"
    },
    "attributes": {
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      "author": "your_username",
      "created_at": "2026-07-20T12:34:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-07-20T12:34:56Z"
    }
  }
}
```
